chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ali bin Mahziyar, who said:

Al-Hasan bin Saeed wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'A man entered into Ihram without Ghusl or without Salat, knowingly or out of ignorance; what is upon him regarding that, and what is befitting that he should do?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'He should repeat.'

key_terms.إحرام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who enters Ihram without Ghusl or Salat?
ai.summary: In this epistle from Imam al-Hassan al-Askari (peace be upon him), the specific legal ruling for a pilgrim who enters the state of Ihram without the prerequisite Ghusl or Salat is clarified as requiring repetition (I'ad), regardless of whether the omission was due to ignorance or knowledge. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the validity of the ritual state being contingent upon the completion of its foundational pillars, distinguishing it from mere sunnah acts. The correspondence format highlights the scholarly practice of resolving specific fiqh queries through direct written transmission from the Imams.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Mahziyar who said,

‘Al-Hassan Bin Saeed wrote to Abu Al-Hassanasws, ‘A man wears Ihraam without washing, or without a Prayer, knowingly or out of ignorance, what is upon him regarding that, and what is befitting that he should be doing?’ So heasws wrote: ‘Repeat’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Mahziyar who has said the following:

“Once al-Hassan ibn Sa‘id wrote to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who assumes the state of Ihram without Ghusl (bath) or without Salat (prayer) knowingly, or is ignorant, and what he owes and what should he do? He (the Imam) wrote in answer, ‘He must assume the state of Ihram again.’”
